Playbook.name: AD – Account Created / Enabled - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1136.002 Create Account Domain Account
MITRE ATT and CK T1098 Account Manipulation

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A domain or local account was created (4720) or a previously disabled account was re-enabled (4722) in the INTDOM environment. The triage question is whether this is an authorised joiner/mover provisioning action, or an attacker planting a backdoor account or re-activating a dormant account to establish persistence. The strongest signal is not the creation itself but what happens next: the same actor elevating the new account into a privileged group, or the new account authenticating within minutes.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A rogue or re-enabled account in a banking domain is durable persistence that survives password resets on other accounts and blends into normal logon traffic. If elevated, it grants an attacker a clean, attributable-looking identity for lateral movement and fraud.

Assets.AssetType: Windows member servers and workstations (local account creation)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing (Account Management subcategory) shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live: 4720/4722/4724/4726/4738 present in the last 30 days).
winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName (actor) and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName (created/enabled account) are populated keyword fields (verified live).

Signal.Name: Account created
Signal.Details: event.code 4720 - a user account was created; TargetUserName is the new account, SubjectUserName is the actor.

Signal.Name: Account enabled
Signal.Details: event.code 4722 - a previously disabled account was enabled; re-activation of a dormant account is a common persistence move.

Signal.Name: Create-then-elevate sequence
Signal.Details: 4720/4722 followed by 4728/4732/4756 (added to a security-enabled group) or an immediate 4624 logon by the same account within the window.

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: The account that was created or enabled (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName from the alert).

Input.name: $actor_user
Input.description: The account that performed the action (winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName from the alert).

Input.name: $host
Input.description: Host/DC that recorded the account-management event (host.name from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: event.code (4720 create vs 4722 enable) and event.action from the alert

InitialAssessment.Rule: If $actor_user is a known IAM/service-desk provisioning identity AND the new account matches the standard naming convention AND no privileged-group add or logon follows, lean False Positive (authorised provisioning).

If $actor_user is a human admin acting outside a change window, OR the new account is added to a privileged group, OR it authenticates within the window, escalate and treat as potential backdoor persistence.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the creation/enable of $target_user was an authorised provisioning action or attacker-planted persistence, and whether the account was elevated or used.

Step.name: Reconstruct the lifecycle of the target account
Step.Purpose: Establish the sequence and actors around $target_user: a create (4720) immediately followed by enable (4722), password set (4723/4724) and group adds in seconds is the rogue-account signature; a lone 4720 by a provisioning identity is routine.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4720","4722","4723","4724","4725","4726","4738","4728","4732","4756","4767","4781") | STATS events=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), last_seen=MAX(@timestamp), actors=VALUES(winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY event.code, event.action | SORT event.code ASC | LIMIT 100
Step.AnalystNotes: 4720 then 4722/4724/4728 within seconds from one actor = provisioned-and-armed account. 4722 alone (enable of an old account) with no prior 4720 in history = dormant-account re-activation, investigate why it was re-enabled.

Step.name: Profile the actor's account-management activity
Step.Purpose: One actor creating/enabling many accounts, or an actor who is not a known provisioning identity, changes this from routine to suspicious.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$actor_user" AND event.code IN ("4720","4722","4725","4726","4738","4728","4732","4724") | STATS actions=COUNT(*), targets=COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), touched=VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), codes=VALUES(event.code), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A single account created by a known service-desk identity = routine. Many targets, or an actor that is a workstation/interactive human outside IT, or an actor that itself was recently created, is a strong escalate signal.

Step.name: Detect create-then-elevate by the same actor
Step.Purpose: The most dangerous pattern is a new account being pushed into a privileged group. This looks at security-enabled group additions the same actor performed in the window.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$actor_user" AND event.code IN ("4728","4732","4756") | STATS adds=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), members=VALUES(winlog.event_data.MemberName), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, event.code | SORT adds DESC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: TargetUserName here is the GROUP; members contains the DN of the account added. If members references $target_user and the group is Domain Admins / Enterprise Admins / a privileged local group, treat as True Positive (backdoor with elevation).

Step.name: Check whether the new account authenticated
Step.Purpose: A brand-new or freshly-enabled account that logs on within the window indicates the account is already in use - the difference between a planted account and an active one.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4624","4768","4769","4776") | STATS logons=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), last_seen=MAX(@timestamp), types=VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), src=VALUES(source.ip), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY event.code | SORT event.code ASC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: Interactive (LogonType 2) or Remote-Interactive (10) logons by a just-created account are high-signal. Kerberos 4768/4769 or NTLM 4776 immediately after creation shows the credential is live. Correlate first_seen here against INV-01 creation time.

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows $target_user (in members) added to a privileged group by $actor_user, OR INV-04 shows the new account authenticating, AND the actor/action is not tied to an approved change record.
Node.Result: True Positive (backdoor / persistence account - escalate to IR immediately)

Node.Condition: INV-01/INV-02 show creation or enable by an actor who is not an authorised provisioning identity, on an unexpected host, or outside a change window, even without elevation yet.
Node.Result: Needs Escalation (unattributed account change - confirm with IAM before closing)

Node.Condition: The action was performed by the documented IAM/service-desk provisioning identity or an admin working under a matching change ticket, the account follows naming standards, and INV-03/INV-04 show no elevation or use.
An automated provisioning/HR-sync connector or a test/lab process is repeatedly creating, enabling or disabling accounts by design and firing this rule as noise.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (tune the rule for the known provisioning source; do not exception broadly)

Node.Condition: Actor or target cannot be attributed from IAM/CMDB, or evidence is mixed (provisioning identity but abnormal elevation).

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised identity created or enabled the account as part of the sanctioned joiner/mover process or an approved change - not a benign guess, an attributable and approved action.

Indicators.Item: $actor_user is the documented IAM/service-desk provisioning account or an admin named on a change ticket covering the window.
New account matches the standard naming convention and OU for its account class.
INV-03 shows no privileged-group add and INV-04 shows no logon by the account.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the change ticket / provisioning request reference.
If a specific provisioning identity is chronically noisy, propose a scoped rule tuning for that actor only.
Close as false_positive with the ticket reference attached.

TruePositive.Definition: An account was created or re-enabled to establish persistence, typically then elevated or used.

Indicators.Item: Create-then-elevate: 4720/4722 followed by a privileged group add (INV-03) referencing $target_user.
New or re-enabled account authenticates within the window (INV-04), especially interactive or remote-interactive.
Actor is an unexpected identity, an unusual host, or itself recently created; action outside any change window.

SOCAction.Item: Disable $target_user and any sibling accounts created by the same actor in the window.
Revoke sessions/tickets for the account; reset the actor account if compromise is suspected.
Open an incident; pull the actor host for forensics; review what the account touched.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An internal automation (HR sync, IDM connector, provisioning script, lab rebuild) creates/enables/disables accounts on a loop as designed - operational noise, not malicious.

Indicators.Item: Same automation actor repeatedly creating/enabling accounts with machine-generated names.
No human actor and no privileged-group elevation.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the automation with its owning team.
Tune the rule for the specific provisioning source; track under detection-tuning, not IR.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If INV-03/INV-04 show elevation or use, disable $target_user immediately and revoke its sessions/tickets.
Identify and freeze any other accounts $actor_user created or enabled in the window (INV-02).

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: If $actor_user is compromised, reset it and audit everything it changed.
Remove the rogue account from any groups it was added to; forensic-triage the actor host.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Review who holds account-creation and group-management rights; enforce change-control on account provisioning.
Add alerting on new accounts added to privileged groups within N minutes of creation.

Escalation.Trigger: Any privileged-group elevation of, or authentication by, a newly created/enabled account; or an account change that cannot be attributed to an approved provisioning process.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Provisioning request or change ticket verified and matches actor, account and window.
INV-03 and INV-04 confirm no elevation and no logon by the account.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Rogue/re-enabled account disabled, removed from all groups, sessions revoked.
Actor account status resolved and root cause (compromise vs insider) documented.
